tagline: Embedding ESG into decision-making and sustainable insurance practices
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the most relevant as it reflects Gjensidige's strategic transformation toward sustainable insurance, aligned with climate and regulatory objectives (EU Taxonomy), a major structural driver in the European insurance sector.
company_description: Gjensidige Forsikring ASA, together with its subsidiaries, provides general insurance and pension products in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia. It operates in four segments: General Insurance Private, General Insurance Commercial, General Insurance Sweden, and Pension. The company offers motor, property, travel, accident and health, general liability, natural perils, agriculture, medical treatment and expense, disability, income protection, workers' compensation, motor vehicle liability, marine, aviation, transport, fire and other damage to property, assistance, other non-life, and life insurance products, as well as non-proportional non-life reinsurance products. It also provides defined contribution occupational pension schemes for businesses, including disability pension, spouse/cohabitant pension, and child's pension; and individual pension savings agreements. The company sells its products to private individuals, commercial and agricultural customers, and private and commercial markets through various distribution channels comprising customer service centres, office channel, call center, Internet, partners, agents, and external brokers. risks.title: Compliance with mandatory ESG/CSRD reporting requirements
risks.summary: Gjensidige is subject to increasing ESG reporting obligations via the CSRD directive and ESRS standards since 2023. Failure to meet targets (e.g., 80% of EU Taxonomy-aligned premiums by 2026, while only ~30% as of end-2023) exposes the company to regulatory non-compliance risks and potential sanctions.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as a reporting obligation since 2023 (CSRD, ESRS), with binding quantitative targets (80% EU Taxonomy by 2026, -55% GHG by 2030). The language is prescriptive and timelines are precise, indicating rising regulatory pressure. Upward trend linked to the acceleration of the European regulatory framework.

risks.title: Climate risk impact on claims and insurance products
risks.summary: Increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events (floods, storms) directly affect Gjensidige's claims experience, particularly on home, vehicle, and commercial property products. The company develops advanced climate models combined with claims data to anticipate these impacts in the short, medium, and long term.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the integration of climate risks into the risk management system, collaboration with the Norwegian Computing Centre to model climate consequences on claims, and damage prevention initiatives. The language highlights an upward trend in extreme weather events directly affecting claims.

risks.title: Supplier dependency and sustainable supply chain risk
risks.summary: Gjensidige relies on external suppliers for its claims management processes (repairs, materials). A supplier non-compliant with ESG standards or experiencing operational failure may disrupt claims settlement and expose the company to reputational risks. The company requires self-declarations and conducts EcoVadis audits to mitigate this risk.
risks.score_rationale: The document describes a supplier screening process via EcoVadis and UN Global Compact self-declarations, indicating operational dependency on third parties for claims processes. The explicit mention of sustainability audits and quarterly monitoring indicates significant exposure to supplier risk in claims settlement operations.

risks.title: Reputational risk from unmet ESG commitments
risks.summary: By publicly committing to multiple international initiatives (UN PRI, SBTi, TCFD, PSI), Gjensidige faces significant reputational risk if ESG targets are not met. The gap between the 80% EU Taxonomy-aligned premium target and the ~30% achieved as of end-2023 illustrates this risk concretely.
risks.score_rationale: Gjensidige has made public, quantified, and binding commitments (SBTi, UN PRI, TCFD, PSI) with specific targets. The observed gap between the 2026 target (80% Taxonomy) and 2023 reality (~30%) creates reputational risk if progress does not accelerate. The language of transparency and accountability amplifies public exposure.

risks.title: Regulatory risk related to EU Taxonomy and product classification
risks.summary: Aligning non-life insurance products with EU Taxonomy criteria represents a major operational challenge for Gjensidige. With only ~30% of eligible premiums aligned as of end-2023 against a 2026 target of 80%, the company must significantly transform its product portfolio (home, vehicle, commercial buildings) under regulatory pressure.
risks.score_rationale: The target of 80% of premiums aligned with the EU Taxonomy by 2026 is a major strategic obligation, with only ~30% achieved as of end-2023. The document positions this risk as a top priority in the Board of Directors' strategy. The evolution of taxonomy criteria (participation in SBTi pilot project 2023/24) indicates ongoing regulatory uncertainty.

risks.title: Nature and biodiversity risk integrated into underwriting
risks.summary: Gjensidige now integrates nature and biodiversity risks into its climate risk assessments, participating since 2024 in UNEP PSI working groups on nature-positive insurance. This emerging risk could affect pricing and underwriting of products covering assets exposed to ecosystem degradation (agriculture, coastal real estate).
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the inclusion of nature risks in climate assessments and participation since 2024 in UNEP PSI working groups on nature-positive insurance. This is an emerging, newly reported risk with exploratory language but a clearly upward trend.

risks.title: Human rights compliance risk across the value chain
risks.summary: Gjensidige faces risks of non-compliance with international human rights standards (UN Global Compact, ILO) through its suppliers and investments. If violations are identified, the company engages in dialogue and may proceed with exclusions, potentially impacting supplier relationships and its investment portfolio.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly cites the integration of UN human rights principles, ILO standards, and OECD guidelines into governing documents, with quarterly monitoring of investments and suppliers. The mention of exclusion mechanisms in case of violations indicates real exposure, although the language remains moderate.
